title: Does Reader::over take paths, readers, or both?
body:
`Reader::over` needs two passes over its sources: a count for `Selection` and a walk. A path can be opened twice. An open reader cannot be rewound.

1. Paths only. Both passes work. Cost: a caller holding open readers cannot use it. No caller in `sail` holds one. stdin is one stream and `sail` already reads it whole.
2. Readers only. Cost: no counting pass, so the caller supplies the count up front.
3. Both. Cost: two constructors with different contracts for one type.

Lean: paths only. A constructor over the parts file from sail-a59d6f can come later as an addition.
close_reason: Decided by Jack: paths only. Both passes reopen each path. A constructor over the parts file from sail-a59d6f can be added later.
